question: Should QQBot permanently reject gateway messages above 1 MiB, or use a larger conservative cap such as the 16 MiB gateway precedent?
rationale: The dependency behavior and need for a bound are proven, but QQ's public gateway contract provides no maximum event size, so repository evidence cannot establish that 1 MiB will never reject legitimate production events.

options.title: Use a 16 MiB cap
options.body: Refresh over current main and use the established gateway headroom while still reducing the dependency default from 100 MiB.

options.title: Keep the 1 MiB cap
options.body: Retain the tighter limit only after a QQBot owner confirms production event-size headroom and accepts fail-closed delivery above that boundary.

recommendation.title: Use a 16 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Refresh over current main and use the established gateway headroom while still reducing the dependency default from 100 MiB.

likelyOwner.reason: The major QQBot gateway architecture history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for channel-specific payload expectations.
